Let
\[
m=da,\qquad n=db,\qquad \gcd(a,b)=1.
\]
Since \(m<n\), we have \(a<b\) not necessarily, but \(b>0\), and \(d>1\). Put
\[
x=t^m,\qquad y=t^n+t^p.
\]

The key cancellation is
\[
y^a-x^b
=(t^n+t^p)^a-t^{mb}.
\]
Because \(an=bd=m b? \) more precisely
\[
an=a(db)=dab=mb,
\]
the leading terms cancel, so
\[
v(y^a-x^b)=an+(p-n)=p+(a-1)n.
\]
Set
\[
q=p+(a-1)n.
\]

I claim the value semigroup of
\[
A=\mathbb C[[x,y]]
\]
is
\[
S=\langle m,n,q\rangle.
\]

Indeed, \(m,n\in S\) come from \(x,y\), and \(q\) comes from \(y^a-x^b\). Conversely, any cancellation among lowest terms of a series in \(x,y\) is caused by the unique binomial relation between the initial monomials \(X\mapsto t^m,\ Y\mapsto t^n\), namely
\[
Y^a-X^b,
\]
since \(\gcd(a,b)=1\). Replacing each such cancelled factor by \(y^a-x^b\) raises the value from \(an\) to \(q\). Iterating shows every possible value is of the form
\[
im+jn+kq,
\]
so \(v(A\setminus\{0\})=\langle m,n,q\rangle\).

For a one-branch subring of \(\mathbb C[[t]]\), the colength
\[
\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[[t]]/A
\]
equals the number of nonnegative integers missing from its value semigroup.

Now compute the genus of
\[
S=\langle da,db,q\rangle.
\]
Since \(\gcd(d,q)=1\), the Apéry set of \(S\) modulo \(m=da\) is
\[
\operatorname{Ap}(S;m)=
\{\,jn+kq:0\le j<a,\ 0\le k<d\,\}.
\]
These \(ad=m\) elements give distinct residues modulo \(m\), and each is minimal in its residue class.

Thus
\[
\sum_{w\in\operatorname{Ap}(S;m)}w
=
d\sum_{j=0}^{a-1}jn
+
a\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}kq
=
\frac{ad(a-1)n}{2}+\frac{ad(d-1)q}{2}.
\]
For a numerical semigroup with multiplicity \(m\),
\[
\#(\mathbb N\setminus S)
=
\frac1m\sum_{w\in\operatorname{Ap}(S;m)}w-\frac{m-1}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\dim_{\mathbb C}\frac{\mathbb C[[t]]}{A}
=
\frac{(a-1)n+(d-1)q-m+1}{2}.
\]
Substituting \(a=m/d\) and \(q=p+(a-1)n\),
\[
\frac{(a-1)n+(d-1)\bigl(p+(a-1)n\bigr)-m+1}{2}
=
\frac{(m-d)n+(d-1)p-m+1}{2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \dim_{\mathbb C}\frac{\mathbb C[[t]]}{A}
=\frac{(m-d)n+(d-1)p-m+1}{2}}
\]
